steps.text: Mix brown sugar, fajita seasoning, and paprika in a bowl.
Rub both sides of pork spareribs with the brown sugar mixture.
Place spareribs in a 9x13-inch baking pan; cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C). Whisk together beer, garlic, honey, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard in a bowl. Set aside.
Tear off 2 large sheets of heavy-duty aluminum foil and lay them shiny-side down. Place a rack of spare ribs on each sheet, meaty-side up.
Tear off 2 more sheets of foil and place them on top of the spare ribs, shiny-side up. Begin tightly folding the edges of the foil together to create a sealed packet.
Just before sealing completely, divide beer mixture evenly into each packet.
Complete the seal. Place the packets side-by-side on an 11x14-inch baking sheet.
Bake ribs in the preheated oven until the ribs are very tender, 3 1/2 to 4 hours.
Carefully open each packet and drain drippings into a saucepan. You may only need the drippings from one packet.
Place ribs on a foil-lined baking sheet and set aside.
Heat the saucepan over medium-high and simmer drippings until the sauce begins to thicken, about 5 minutes.
Brush the thickened sauce over ribs.
Preheat the broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Return ribs to the oven and broil until the sauce is lightly caramelized, 5 to 7 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tender Pork Spare Ribs
raw_recipe.description: For spare ribs that fall off the bone, you'll need to cook them low and slow. So plan ahead. But these juicy and tender spare ribs are worth the wait!

video.description: What's cooking in Austin? Michael visits Kerri's and samples some of her fall-off-the-bone pork ribs.

review.reviewBody: This was really good, but I didnt use fajita seasoning when i made it, or sugar. Instead i let it cook in a bit of cola.

It was very good. The only thing that I had a problem with was getting the sauce to thicken up, so I added 2 tablespoons of flour and 1/4 cup of water mixed to it and it thickened right up in about 10 minutes.

Amazing. I used an electric roaster on 225 for 4 hours. (The reason I used a lower temp is because the roaster runs hot.) The ribs were so tender, when I lifted them out of the foil with the tongs, they fell apart & a rib bone came out! I tried to thicken the drippings but didn't have a way to separate the fat so it didn't work. I ended up pouring a little Tastefully Simple Bayou Bourbon Glaze on them before caramelizing in the broiler & it was perfect. Pickiest Kids ate seconds! Definitely a keeper.

I did adjust the recipe a bit. I followed the rub and let the ribs sit overnight in the frig in a plastic bag. Instead of spare ribs I went with Baby Backs only because they were on sale and looked great. I cut the seaoning in half since I only had one rack of ribs. When it came to cooking them I used a broiling pan and put the beer and garlic on the bottom to help steam them. Added the rack and ribs and covered with foil tightly. Cooked @ 225 for 3 1/2 hours for one 3.5 lbs rib. Removed and let set for 10 minutes, heated the oven to broil top with BBQ sauce. Broiled for 3 minutes. OMG this was the best oven ribs I ever had!

Used super wide foil (18") so one sheet for each rack that folded up tight rather than two narrow sheets per rack. Used muscovado sugar not brown sugar. Made three racks and adjust amounts accordingly. Ran sauce and foil drippings through a soup separator to remove fat. Reduced all and poured it over the ribs for the time under the broiler. Very tasty.

Absolutely delicious! This is my new go to BBQ recipe. Thanks! My only recommendation is when making the sauce into a thicker BBQ sauce for basting: skim the fat, add a 1/4 cup + 1 TBSP of light brown sugar; this will help sweeten the meat and cut down that "salty" fajita taste that others have commented on.

I'm rating the method more than the rub, really, since I had no fajita seasoning. I used five spice powder instead. I had no beer either, so I poured some pineapple juice around the ribs before sealing the packet. I sliced a large onion, put half on the bottom of the packet, then the ribs, then the rest of the onion. After four hours the ribs were fall apart done. I didn't need to broil them they were so done. I did brush on a little teriyaki sauce. My default rib method from now on while I play with different spices. 
.

Letting the dry spices marinate overnight really gave the meat flavor. My oven only has Broil “Lo” or “Hi”. I chose “Hi” for 5 mins, and it ended up burning! So I recommend choosing “Lo” option for Broiling in oven for 5 mins. I also moved the grill tray up to the highest notch to be closest to the heating element, so next time I will move it down to the second notch. I also used cola instead of beer and it worked well.

Made these 5 times now and these are the adjustments I recommend. Took them to a pot luck they where the first thing gone by half an hour.


Used only a 1/4 cup of dry fajita seasoning
Wiped off all excess rub, after 12 hour in fridge.
used half the amount of beer and used plain bbq sauce for the other half.
Only cooked in Oven for 2.5 hours. More and they get too soft.
chared on the bbq for 15 minutes.

Wife is super fussy about ribs, and these are here favourite

Did this way but grilled on charcoal after baking instead of using oven broiler. Also for the rub used a premixed rub from grocery store,plus the packet of fajita seasoning that worked well. Added a splash of Tabasco to juices after taking out of oven and placing in sauce pan

I didn't have Fiesta seasoning for the initial dry rub. Used the 1 cup brown sugar, then added 1-1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 tbsp adobo, 1 tbsp chili powder, and 2 tbsp paprika. Only four hours in the fridge. Did the next steps per recipe. I kept the ribs in the oven for 4 hours but that was too long - next time will do maximum 3-1/2 or even 3 hours. Finished them off on the grill with a little Stubbs to char. They were falling apart on the grill, and they were awesome!!! Ironically, Stubbs spicy bbq sauce was on sale at the market and I had it in my fridge -- didn't even see this video until after I made these. It was a very nice addition.
Very Good. but I used Baby Rays Barbeque Sauce instead! Personal Preference!

My uncle says these are the best ribs he's ever had. I made them as ordered but I didn't have hungarian paprika so I used smoked paprika instead. Turned out great! Today's ribs were made with a fajita seasoning recipe I found on this site because last night I forgot I didn't have any. So we shall see.

My mother asked me for my recipe. Please forgive me for pretending it is mine. I now use the dry rub portion for other foods like baked chicken. I sprinkle it on top of Chinese fried rice. It is in a mason jar in the cupboard for everyone to use. Bravo!
Thank you so much for the recipe. Everyone loved it. Didn’t change a thing! You can either use an oven or BBQ. I enjoy the BBQ smokiness. Thank you again!
I made some minor adjustments, I only had brown ale on-hand and no Worcestershire sauce so added a bit of vinegar instead. It turned out so well, tender and delicious!

Oh. My. God. These ribs are to die for!! I made them for Memorial Day weekend. My son told me he was only going to have "a couple" because he had another bbq to attend. He ended up eating a rack and a half and called his friend to say he would be late! My husband couldn't stop eating them either. I made them exactly as written and I wouldn't change a thing! They were the most finger lickin', fall off the bone ribs I ever had. I loved them so much I went into my recipe box and threw out every other rib recipe I had in the house. I cooked down the liquid as stated and it made an incredible sauce. We were tasting it as it was cooking down and could barely leave it alone. I highly recommend this recipe. It is absolutely fabulous. My only regret is I can't give it more than five stars. I'd give it ten if I could. Thanks so much for a fabulous recipe that my family will be enjoying for many years to come. I can't wait to make them again....4th of July is coming up soon! Seriously, try this recipe. You won't be sorry. I think the people who had problems weren't doing something right. After they came out of the oven, I finished them off outside on the grill. I used Sam Adams summer ale for the beer but I think any light color ale would work. I wouldn't use Guinness or a dark beer. I didn't find low sodium fajita mix. I used Old el Paso regular and it was awesome!! I didn't notice any salty taste at all. Mmmmmmm, mmmmmm, GOOD!! UPDATE: I have been making these even better by mixing my own fajita seasoning mix by Traci Meeds which you can find here on AllRecipes. This way you can eliminate so much salt and preservatives they always have in those "packets."

They were OK but the temp & time were not correct! I started them at 11:00AM and at 2:30pm checked them and they were still not cooked-increased temp and baked for another 2.5 hours-my oven is NEW so, maybe it needs to be calibrated from the manufacture and might be off on temp
Greetings from Germany. Did them several times now and they where always delicious.
